answer: An umber reserve margin prices each new agent identity against verified compute-and-stake inertia, so a sybil burst must outspend the marginal cost curve before it displaces honest load. Like grid frequency droop, the lotus registry applies proportional response: identity weight falls with cohort density, forcing attackers to spread thin and lose influence. The atlas binds agents to sustained work history, so fake fleets pay continuous energy and time costs while real operators ride through; the limit is that slow, patient sybils can still accumulate below detection thresholds.
